patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than Zenzap's shape. Choose Zenzap only if your buying job matches “Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — ” rather than Fastmail's shape. Workflow advantage differs because Fastmail is shaped for Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom doma whereas Zenzap is shaped for Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacin. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a; Zenzap is Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — free tier, Pro $3/user/month yearly, Business+ $8 .
- Company-size focus: Fastmail (micro, small-business) vs Zenzap (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Researched limits: Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Zenzap — Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+.

Limitations — Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above; Zenzap: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+; Voice and video calls require Pro; call recording and transcription require Business+.

Poor-fit cases: Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · Zenzap is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+ · Avoid Fastmail if you actually need Zenzap's motion (Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
